newsitem.title: USA: Clinton picks prosecutor for top U.S. Justice post.
newsitem.headline: Clinton picks prosecutor for top U.S. Justice post.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has selected local U.S. Attorney Eric Holder for the Justice Department's second-highest job, Attorney Genderal Janet Reno said on Thursday.

If confirmed by the Senate as deputy attorney general, Holder would succeed Jamie Gorelick, who announced in January she would be leaving to spend more time with her family. Holder would be the first black to serve in the senior post.

At her weekly news briefing, Reno hailed Clinton's nomination of Holder, a veteran prosecutor and a former judge. "I think he will bring tremendous abilities to this job ... He is one of the finest people I know."
White House spokesman Mike McCurry said of Holder, "He is one of the finest U.S. attorneys anywhere in the country and the president has a great deal of confidence in him."
Holder was recommended to the White House by Reno several weeks ago and had always been the top contender for the job, Justice Department officials said.

As the No. 2 person at the Justice Department, he would be in charge of running the day-to-day operations of the agency. As deputy attorney general, he would play a key role in supervising the Justice Department's investigation into questionable Democratic campaign fund-raising activities and a decision on whether to seek an independent counsel.

Holder, the top prosecutor in Washington, D.C., was a former Justice Department lawyer who worked in its elite public integrity unit, handling corruption cases. As a Justice Department prosecutor for 12 years starting in 1976, he prosecuted a number of high-profile cases.
The son of immigrants from Barbados, Holder grew up in New York City and graduated from Columbia University and its law school.
